category_summary:
### Executive Signal
- The agent ecosystem is fragmenting into specialized toolchains (skills, harnesses, humanizers) while BYOK/local-inference repos signal a **sovereignty-first procurement shift**. Treat AI agents as a stack to assemble, not a product to buy.
### Priority Developments
- **Agent skill/harness stack emerges** — ECC, [mattpocock/skills](/?date=2026-09-07&category=github_trending#item-e0c58594c75a), [ponytail](/?date=2026-09-07&category=github_trending#item-f6f7996805e6), and diagram-design cluster around enhancing Claude Code, Codex, Cursor; agent quality now depends on reusable skills and memory, not raw model power.
- **BYOK and local inference reach enterprise viability** — [Experiential](/?date=2026-09-07&category=github_trending#item-86ad4161107a) (1000+ models) and [Magnitude](/?date=2026-09-07&category=github_trending#item-a8ca364ba554) (local inference) signal demand for model portability to cut costs and escape vendor lock-in.
- **Open-source coding agents are commoditizing** — [OpenCode](/?date=2026-09-07&category=github_trending#item-df9e634e59f2) and Hermes Agent challenge proprietary tooling; evaluation and governance frameworks become the new differentiator.
- **AI-output humanization forms a category** — [Humanizer](/?date=2026-09-07&category=github_trending#item-4c47dd9e0572) treats AI text as detectable content; regulated industries will need provenance and authenticity tooling.
### Leadership Implications
- **Mandate a 60-day agent stack review**: inventory skill libraries, select a BYOK gateway, and assign owners for agent evaluation and security.
- **Re-evaluate inference procurement** against open-source local-orchestration; credible alternatives now exist for reducing vendor concentration risk.
